fish.name: Button Smelt
fish.flavor: Small, silver, and exactly the size of the button missing from your favorite coat. It is not that button, and it resents the question.

fish.name: Sock Eel
fish.flavor: Lurks in tidepools looking exactly like a lost woolen sock. Somewhere out there, a very cold foot is owed an apology.

fish.name: Doodle Dab
fish.flavor: Its back is covered in scribbles that no two scholars read the same way. The dab itself insists the work is abstract.

fish.name: Teacup Flounder
fish.flavor: Small enough to nap in a teacup and rude enough to try. Serve with lemon only if you want to be haunted.

fish.name: Grinning Goby
fish.flavor: Nobody knows what it is so pleased about. Frankly, the not-knowing is the worst part.

fish.name: Sea Biscuit
fish.flavor: Round, buttery-gold, and dense as regret. Old beachcombers claim dunking one in tea is good luck; the biscuit disagrees.

fish.name: Whistling Sprat
fish.flavor: Whistles one clear note at dusk, always slightly flat. Choirs of them have driven lighthouse keepers into early retirement.

fish.name: Penny Skipper
fish.flavor: Skips across the shallows like a flung coin. Make a wish anyway — it hasn't said no yet.

fish.name: Beachcomber Blenny
fish.flavor: Hoards bottle caps, shell shards, and one very specific pebble it will not discuss. A kindred spirit, honestly.

fish.name: Dune Gudgeon
fish.flavor: Lives in the warm puddles between dunes and considers this a bold lifestyle choice. The dune grass whispers about it.

fish.name: Bashful Bream
fish.flavor: Blushes rose-gold the moment it is caught. Compliment it once and it will follow your boat for a week.

fish.name: Foam Nibbler
fish.flavor: Eats sea foam and nothing else. Naturalists call this impossible; the nibbler calls it a light lunch.

fish.name: Pocket Herring
fish.flavor: Folklore says one in your pocket brings small change and smaller luck. Both claims check out.

fish.name: Wobble Wrasse
fish.flavor: Swims like it is perpetually stepping off a boat. Endearing for the first hour.

fish.name: Kelpie Minnow
fish.flavor: Foals of the kelpie, say the old songs — or just a minnow with a dramatic mane. Either way, do not accept a ride.

fish.name: Saltlick Mullet
fish.flavor: Follows the tide in to lick the salt off drying rocks. Has opinions about your seasoning.

fish.name: Gull-Mocker
fish.flavor: Imitates gull cries so well that the gulls have started imitating it back. The beach has become extremely loud.

fish.name: Fortune Sole
fish.flavor: The speckles on its back rearrange into tomorrow's weather, next week's news, and once, somebody's wedding date. It charges in shrimp.

fish.name: Driftwood Mimic
fish.flavor: Indistinguishable from a weathered plank until it blinks. Many a beach bonfire has apologized to one.

fish.name: Bottlepost Eel
fish.flavor: Swallows message-bottles and delivers them, eventually, to roughly the right person. Postage is one squid, no refunds.

fish.name: Purse Pilferer
fish.flavor: A pocket-sized shark that steals mermaids' purses off the wrack line and stashes them in crab burrows. The mermaids are furious. The crabs are confused.

fish.name: Hourglass Herring
fish.flavor: The pale sand inside it runs out precisely at slack tide, then flips. Nobody has explained how it knows, or why it bothers.

fish.name: Tidepool Gossip
fish.flavor: Presses up against the rim of every tidepool like a neighbor at a fence. Knows what the anemone did. Will tell you.

fish.name: Sighing Sanddab
fish.flavor: Exhales one long, contented sigh whenever the tide comes in. It isn't sad. It's just a lot, you know?

fish.name: Two-Penny Turbot
fish.flavor: Bears two coin-bright spots that shopkeepers swear are legal tender. Two-penny turbot; priceless attitude.

fish.name: Widow's Knot Eel
fish.flavor: Ties itself into the same knot sailors' wives once tied into their shawls to hold the weather kind. Untying one is considered extremely rude.

fish.name: Selkie's Comb
fish.flavor: Slim and pearl-toothed, said to be the comb a selkie dropped when she chose to live ashore. Hold it to your ear and you'll hear someone humming, far off and happy.

fish.name: Backwards Barracuda
fish.flavor: Swims only in reverse and consequently arrives everywhere yesterday. It has already been caught by you; it seemed pleased about it.

fish.name: Saltwitch Sculpin
fish.flavor: Warty, bearded, and muttering. Leave it a grub on a flat rock and your boots will stay dry for a season — that's the deal, don't push it.

fish.name: Foglantern Ray
fish.flavor: Glides along the shore on misty nights, glowing gently at the edges. Ships steer by it, and it has never once led them wrong — which deeply unsettles the lighthouse union.

fish.name: Weeping Conger
fish.flavor: Cries endlessly into the sea for reasons it has never shared. Old salts say that's where the ocean gets it.

fish.name: Ninth-Wave Dancer
fish.flavor: Rides only the ninth wave of every set — the big one, the storyteller's wave. Between waves nobody knows where it goes, and it refuses to be followed.

fish.name: Message-in-a-Bream
fish.flavor: Every single one contains a tiny rolled-up note. Most say things like 'hello' or 'lovely weather.' One said 'behind you,' and that fisher has not returned to the beach.

fish.name: The Cartographer's Regret
fish.flavor: Its markings form a flawless map of a coastline no chart has ever shown. Sailors who follow it come home years later — tanned, quiet, and unwilling to say where.

fish.name: Widow of the Shallows
fish.flavor: Drifts through the moonlit surf in a long veil of trailing fins, keeping a vigil older than the pier. It watches the horizon. It is always watching the horizon.

fish.name: Saint Elmo's Herald
fish.flavor: Comes crackling ashore ahead of the storm, wearing the same cold fire that dances on mastheads. Catching one means the lightning knows your name — kindly, for now.

fish.name: The Hush Between Waves
fish.flavor: That perfect silence just after one wave falls and before the next begins — this fish lives there. Hold it, and for a single heartbeat the whole coast holds its breath with you.

fish.name: The Drowned Bellringer
fish.flavor: A chapel sank off this coast three hundred years ago, and something still rings its bell at low tide. Landing it fills your ears with bronze and your heart with a Sunday you never lived.

fish.name: Grandmother Undertow
fish.flavor: Every child on this coast is warned about her, and every child is right. She pulls with the patience of someone who has raised a thousand tides and buried a hundred piers — yet she has never kept a swimmer who asked nicely to go home.

fish.name: The Tide That Remembers
fish.flavor: The sea forgets nothing; it simply keeps it all in one fish. In its scales you glimpse every footprint the tide ever smoothed away — and there, small and bright among them, your own.
